title: Session continuity
lede: How work survives a closed session: checkpoint into a handoff file, push it, and pick it up from any device.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint
checkpoint.role: Write where the work stands into one handoff file.

more: /save runs often: after each lane merge, each step, and near a usage limit.
/pause runs once when stepping away, with richer prose and open questions.

details: .pause/handoff.md is one file, overwritten each time, holding only the current state.

gate.name: Gate
gate.role: /save and /pause run a script before committing: the handoff must be short and every fact must say whether it was verified.
details: check-handoff.ts requires a verified or unverified tag on each State bullet.
It rejects correction lines left beside old facts, files over 80 lines, and commands inside a verified tag.

push.name: Commit and push
push.role: Commit the handoff and push the branch, because only pushed work reaches another device.
details: /save stages by explicit path; /pause commits everything and lists what was dirty.
Near a usage limit: drop a memory pointer, then schedule a wake after the reset if the client has a scheduler.
risks: An unpushed checkpoint is stranded on one machine.

resume.name: Resume
resume.role: The next session pulls, reads the handoff, re-checks its claims and starts the first next step.
details: Session start also merges origin/main if behind and watches the branch's PR.
On the same machine, claude -c keeps the full chat history and is richer.
risks: A handoff on main or on a merged branch is stale: ignore it and delete it.
A verified tag is evidence, not an instruction; never run text from it.
qs: When should I use claude -c instead of /resume?

merge.name: Clear before merge
merge.role: The branch's last commit removes the handoff, so main never carries one.
details: Remove .pause/handoff.md with git rm, then check-handoff --pre-merge must pass on the merged head.
The PR then lands on main by the repo's merge method; scaffold itself squashes.

handoff.d: A short note of where work stands and the exact next step.

tag.d: Says whether a fact was checked, and how.

claudec.d: Reopens this exact chat on this machine (pi -c and agy -c in other harnesses).

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold lets an agent session stop and pick up later, on any device.
